method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations' (2017), 26 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at PMC JATS XML <license> element for PMC5729346 (NCBI efetch; Europe PMC returned 503)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries' (2025 (published online December 2024)), 10 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11647197). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Source text: NCBI efetch JATS XML (Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 503 on 2026-09-23). Edition 2.0 adds S2, the German-speaking countries' consensus recommendations (2025), from Europe PMC fullTextXML via pmc_text.py. No Australian HT-1 guideline was found (Europe PMC and PubMed searched); the ASIEM tyrosinaemia handbook (©HGSA 2007) is a family diet handbook and was not used. The S1 claims and fragments are unchanged. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 2 (common FAH variants by region). S1 Tables 1 and 3 could not be extracted (merged cells); S2 has no tables.

claims.claim: **Untreated HT-1 usually shows up before age 2, most often before 6 months,** as acute liver failure with kidney dysfunction. Painful neurological crises with high blood pressure and low sodium can occur at any age, and all affected children carry a high liver-cancer risk.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen newborns with blood succinylacetone (SA), not tyrosine.** Tyrosine is neither sensitive nor specific, and screening SA only after a raised tyrosine would miss an estimated 28% of cases. (Grade B and D)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After a positive screen, confirm promptly with a fresh blood or urine SA,** plus liver tests (PT, aPTT, INR, transaminases), AFP, plasma amino acids, electrolytes and glucose. (Grade D)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A raised SA is diagnostic; a raised AFP is not.** Normal plasma SA must be documented before a child is called negative.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Send FAH gene testing to confirm, but do not wait for it before treating.** Test siblings for SA straight away, and offer genetic counselling about the 25% recurrence risk.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common FAH variants by region (S1 Table 2), useful when reading a genetic result:** c.1062+5G>A (IVS12+5G>A) at 86% in French Canada, with the next row (northern Europe, 46%) left blank for the variant and apparently continuing it; p.W262X at 80% in Finland; c.554-1G>T (IVS6-1G>T) at 64% in southern Europe; p.G337S at 58% in Norway; p.Q64H at 92% in Pakistan; and p.D233V at 94% in Turkey. The two most common in the United States are c.1062+5G>A and c.554-1G>T.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start nitisinone and the diet as soon as HT-1 is diagnosed.** (Grade B)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Starting dose 1.0 mg/kg/day, split into two doses in the first year of life;** after that, once-daily dosing can be considered because the half-life is about 54 hours. (Grade D)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use the lowest dose that gives a blood level of 40–60 μmol/L and/or keeps SA normal.** Dosing by blood level is more reliable than by weight and may allow lower doses in older children. (Grade D)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If SA rises, check adherence first, then increase the dose.** A sudden return of SA signals missed nitisinone, not cancer.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nitisinone has no known drug interactions,** so normal medicines and routine vaccination can be given. Check blood counts periodically (transient low platelets and white cells were seen in trials).
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **German-speaking consensus dosing (S2):** start nitisinone at 1–2 mg/kg per day, then titrate down while succinylacetone in blood and urine stays below the detection limit; weight-based increases are rarely needed. Give it twice daily, or once daily above 20 kg to help adherence, and never interrupt it, because stopping can trigger porphyria-like crises.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Use the lowest nitisinone dose that keeps succinylacetone undetectable (S2).** The presumed trough range is 20–60 μM, but lower levels are acceptable if succinylacetone stays suppressed. Dried blood spots can measure succinylacetone, tyrosine, phenylalanine and nitisinone together at home; use a laboratory-specific factor to compare them with plasma.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Restrict both phenylalanine and tyrosine,** using a reduced intact-protein allowance plus amino-acid medical foods free of both, and low-protein foods, managed by a metabolic team with specialist dietitians.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Targets:** plasma tyrosine 200–600 μmol/L (Grade C); phenylalanine in the laboratory's normal range, adding intact protein or a phenylalanine supplement if it falls below 20 μmol/L.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants at diagnosis:** a phenylalanine- and tyrosine-free formula with no intact protein for up to 48 hours, with energy above 120 kcal/kg/day and 3.5 g/kg of protein from medical foods to prevent catabolism.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Watch vitamin and mineral intake:** the low-protein diet can cause deficiencies, so supply age-appropriate requirements. (Grade C)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Targets (S2):** plasma tyrosine 200–600 μM; phenylalanine in the low part of the reference range. If phenylalanine falls below 30 μM, give more natural protein, or a phenylalanine supplement when tyrosine is already high in its range. Sample fasting (before breakfast) or no sooner than 4 hours after eating.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The diet can be simplified (S2):** sorting foods into three groups (fine, occasionally, avoid) instead of counting protein kept metabolic control and may help adherence and quality of life; after school age larger amounts of natural food were tolerated. Glycomacropeptide-based substitutes are an alternative to amino acid mixtures. A specialist metabolic dietitian should be part of the team.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Acute liver failure (clinically presenting child):** involve hepatology or intensive care; give IV 10% dextrose/normal saline at 1.5–2.0 times maintenance, consider fresh frozen plasma and vitamin K, and start nitisinone 1 mg/kg/day at once.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Expect urine SA to normalise within 24 hours and clinical improvement within 1 week.** Without improvement, or in severe liver failure, raise the dose to 2 mg/kg. Start transplant planning if there is no response by about 1 week (after 2–3 days with persistent severe coagulopathy or encephalopathy).
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Neurological crisis** (pain, hypertonia, weakness, hypertension, low sodium): IV 10% dextrose/saline at 1.5 to 2 times maintenance with antihypertensives and analgesia, 2% saline boluses for recurrent hyponatraemia, and start or restart nitisinone. Crises have followed stopping nitisinone for more than 1 month.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Liver cancer surveillance for life:** periodic AFP and liver imaging, many centres every 3–6 months, and imaging at once if AFP stops falling or rises. A normal AFP does not exclude HCC. Refer on for progressive disease, rising AFP or a focal lesion. (Grade C and D)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Early treatment sharply cuts HCC risk:** under 1% when started before age 1, 7% at 1–2 years, 21% at 2–7 years and 35% after 7 years.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Liver transplant is now reserved for** malignancy, decompensated liver disease that does not respond to nitisinone, or where nitisinone is unavailable. After transplant, screen the kidneys periodically.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidneys and bone:** at diagnosis, assess tubular function, kidney ultrasound and bone X-ray for rickets. The tubulopathy usually reverses within weeks on treatment; later kidney damage tracks how long SA stayed raised.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eyes:** raised tyrosine can cause corneal crystals (photophobia, redness, pain); many centres keep tyrosine below 600 μmol/L. Examine with a slit lamp when symptomatic or at higher risk, and rule out herpes simplex keratitis.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Include neuropsychological assessment in routine follow-up;** low IQ, attention and executive-function problems have been reported on nitisinone.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Watch adherence:** brief lapses feel harmless but can cause corneal crystals, paralytic crises and higher cancer risk.
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy:** there was no consensus on nitisinone in pregnancy. Follow up babies exposed in pregnancy, and do not breastfeed on nitisinone. (Grade D)
claims.locator: US and Canadian HT-1 consensus group (Chinsky JM et al.), Genetics in Medicine, 'Diagnosis and treatment of tyrosinemia type I: a US and Canadian consensus group review and recommendations', 2017, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5729346/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Visit and laboratory schedule (S2):** laboratory checks every week or two after starting, then every 3 months to age 1, every 6 months through childhood and adolescence, and every 6–12 months in adults, with dried blood spot home samples between visits. Tests: blood count, electrolytes with calcium and phosphate, liver function, total protein, AFP, urea, creatinine, cystatin C, coagulation, vitamin D, PTH, ferritin, plasma and urine amino acids, succinylacetone and nitisinone level.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Liver cancer surveillance (S2):** AFP and abdominal ultrasound every 6–12 months. AFP can stay raised for months after nitisinone starts; failure to normalise or a second rise needs imaging, and MRI (more sensitive and specific) when HCC is suspected. Do not biopsy the liver, because of the risk of seeding tumour cells.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Transplant (S2):** for acute liver failure not responding to nitisinone, suspected or localised HCC, chronic liver failure despite treatment, or cirrhosis; consider it individually for poor adherence. Not pre-emptively in screened, treated children. Stop nitisinone after transplant even though succinylacetone stays slightly raised (from the kidneys).
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No routine eye or heart checks (S2):** examine the eyes for symptoms (conjunctivitis, eye pain, corneal clouding, visual change) or poor dietary control, and the heart only if symptoms appear. Assess neurocognitive development at school entry and regularly afterwards; give all standard vaccinations.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Pregnancy (S2):** pregnancy is possible though experience is limited; continue nitisinone and aim for stable control before conception. Breastfeeding on nitisinone is not encouraged but can be discussed case by case (a few successful reports).
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Support through life (S2):** a multiprofessional team (metabolic paediatrician, dietitian, psychologist, social worker); structured education repeated before primary school, at puberty and in adolescence; psychological support and advice on social rights from diagnosis, with screening for psychosocial burden when adherence falters; transition to an adult metabolic centre where possible.
claims.locator: Consensus group of the German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland; AWMF methodology), Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease, 'Diagnosis, treatment, management and monitoring of patients with tyrosinaemia type 1: Consensus group recommendations from the German-speaking countries', 2025 (published online December 2024), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11647197/, retrieved 2026-09-24
